editorial_note: Śrīdhara's own commentary, not the Bhāgavatam-verse synonyms. Retains odd readings in the pinned witness; footnotes, Madhva, Jīva, Viśvanātha and Baladeva are not silently inserted as Śrīdhara. No full-canto or independent printed-edition verification is claimed.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं प्रथमेऽध्याये षट् प्रश्ना मुनिभिः कृताः । द्वितीये तूत्तरं सूतश् चतुर्णाम् आह तेष्व् अथ ॥ विप्राणाम् इत्य् एवं-भूतैः सम्यक् प्रश्नैः हृष्टो रोमहर्षणस्य पुत्र उग्रश्रवास् तेषां वचः प्रतिपूज्य सत्-कृत्य प्रवक्तुम् उपचक्रमे उप्रक्रान्तवान् ॥१॥
word_for_word: by proper questions of this kind
entries.literal_english: Thus, the sages posed six questions in the first chapter; in the second Sūta now answers four of them. Ugraśravas, Romaharṣaṇa's son, was delighted by these fitting questions of the brahmins. Having honored their words, that is, treated them respectfully, he began to speak.
entries.note: The witness ends with उप्रक्रान्तवान्; the apparent irregularity is noted, not silently corrected.

entries.sanskrit: तत्-कृपालुतां दर्शयन्न् आह—य इति । अन्धं गाढं तमः संसाराख्यम् अतितर्तुम् इच्छताम् । पुराणानां मध्ये गुह्यं गोप्यम् । तत्र हेतुत्वेन चत्वारि विशेषणानि । स्वो निजोऽसाधारणोऽनुभावः प्रभावो यस्य तत्-स्वानुभावम् । अखिल-शास्त्र-श्रुतीनां सारम् । एकम् अद्वितीयम् । अनुपमम् इत्य् अर्थः । आत्मानं कार्य-कारण-सङ्घातम् अधिकृत्य वर्तमानम् आत्म-तत्त्वम् अध्यात्मं तस्य दीपं साक्षात् प्रकाशकम् । उपयामि शरणं व्रजामि ॥३॥
word_for_word: of those wishing to cross completely beyond
of which there is this efficacy
that which possesses its own extraordinary potency
essence of all scripture and revealed teaching
the aggregate of effects and causes
entries.literal_english: Describing [Śuka's] compassion, he begins ‘he who.’ The ‘blinding darkness’ is the dense darkness called saṃsāra, which people wish to cross completely. ‘Secret among the Purāṇas’ means what is guarded. Four qualifiers establish its special character: it has a power uniquely its own; it is the essence of all scripture and revelation; it is one, without a second and incomparable; and it is a lamp directly illuminating the truth about the self, understood here with reference to the aggregate of cause and effect. ‘I approach’ means ‘I seek refuge.’
entries.note: The qualifiers are explained from Śrīdhara's source alone. The much longer Jīva commentary printed after this block is not merged into it.

entries.sanskrit: जयत्य् अनेन संसारम् इति जयो ग्रन्थस् तम् उदीरयेद् इति स्वयं तथोदीरयन्न् अन्यान् पौराणिकान् उपशिक्षयति ॥४॥
word_for_word: by means of this one conquers
entries.literal_english: The scripture is called ‘Jaya’ because by means of it one conquers saṃsāra. The injunction is to recite that text; by reciting it himself, he teaches other Purāṇa reciters to do likewise.

entries.sanskrit: तेषां वचः प्रतिपूज्येति यद् उक्तं तत् प्रतिपूजनं करोति । हे मुनयः ! साधु यथा भवति तथाऽहं पृष्टः । यतो लोकानां मङ्गलम् एतत् । यद् यतः कृष्ण-विषयः संप्रश्नः कृतः । सर्व-शास्त्रार्थ-सारोद्धार-प्रश्नस्यापि कृष्णे पर्यवसानाद् एवम् उक्तम् ॥५॥
word_for_word: even the question seeking to extract the essence of all scripture
it was said in this way
entries.literal_english: The earlier statement that he ‘honored their words’ is fulfilled by this expression of respect: ‘O sages, you have questioned me properly.’ This is for the welfare of the world, because the question concerns Kṛṣṇa. Even the question about extracting the essence of all scripture ultimately culminates in Kṛṣṇa; therefore he speaks in this way.

entries.sanskrit: श्री-गणेशाय नमः । द्वितीये तु दशाध्यायैः श्री-भागवतम् आदितः । उद्देश-लक्षणोक्तिभ्यां सङ्क्षेपेणोपवर्ण्यते ॥इ॥ तत्र तु प्रथमेऽध्याये कीर्तन-श्रवणादिभिः । स्थविष्ठे भगवद्-रूपे मनसो धारणोच्यते ॥इइ॥ यन्-नाम-कीर्तनं दान-तपो-योगादि-सत्-फलम् । तं नित्यं परमानन्दं हरिं नर नम स्मर ॥इइइ॥ अथ द्वितीय-स्कन्ध-व्याख्या । उक्तः पूर्वम् उपोद्घातः सप्रसङ्गः शुकागमः । राज्ञा पृष्टं नॄणां कृत्यम् अथाह शुक-सन्-मुनिः ॥इव्॥ राज्ञः प्रश्नम् अभिनन्दति—वरीयान् इति । ते त्वया । पुंसां श्रोतव्यादिषु मध्ये यः परः श्रेष्ठ-गोचरः प्रश्नः कृत एष वरीयान् । यतो लोक-हितम् एतत्, मोक्ष-हेतुत्वात् । आत्म-विदां मुक्तानां च संमतो यतः ॥१॥
word_for_word: through statements of enumeration and defining characteristics
by praise, hearing and related practices
upon the Lord's vast or gross form
is the good fruit of giving, austerity, yoga and the like
the commentary on the second canto
among things that people should hear and the rest
having the supreme as its subject
the question that has been asked
of those who know the self
entries.literal_english: Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa. In the second canto, the Śrī-Bhāgavata is briefly described from its beginning in ten chapters by statements of its subjects and their definitions. The first chapter teaches fixing the mind on the Lord's great form through chanting, hearing and similar practices. O man, bow to and remember Hari, eternal supreme bliss, the chanting of whose name yields the wholesome fruit of charity, austerity, yoga and the rest. Now begins the explanation of the second canto. The introductory setting, including Śuka's arrival, has already been related. The king asked what people should do; now the holy sage Śuka answers. He commends the king's question with the verse beginning ‘More excellent’: ‘by you’ is the sense of te; the question is especially excellent because, among matters worth hearing, it concerns the highest subject. It benefits the world as a cause of liberation, and it is approved by knowers of the self and liberated persons.
entries.note: The witness includes editor's numbered footnotes and an alternate introductory stanza; neither is inserted into Śrīdhara's primary passage here. Its nonstandard introductory verse numerals इ, इइ, इइइ, इव् are retained.
